TRANSCRIPT OF PROCEEDINGS
THE HON CATHERINE HOLMES AC SC, Commissioner
THE ROYAL COMMISSION INTO THE ROBODEBT SCHEME
MONDAY, 12 DECEMBER 2022 AT 10.01 AM (AEST)
DAY 18
MR JUSTIN GREGGERY KC, Senior Counsel Assisting
MS SALWA MARSH, Counsel Assisting
MR TRENT GLOVER, for the Commonwealth
MR M. PRUSCINO, for the Commonwealth
MR FITZPATRICK, for the Commonwealth

COMMISSIONER: I will take the day's appearances.
MR GREGGERY: If it please the Commission, I appear today with Ms Marsh.
COMMISSIONER: Yes. Mr Glover?
MR GLOVER: If the Commission pleases, today I appear with my learned friends Mr
Fitzpatrick and Mr Pruscino.
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. Would you spell that perhaps?
MR GLOVER: Yes. Certainly. It is P-r-u-s-c-i-n-o.
COMMISSIONER: Thanks very much. Yes, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Yes, Commissioner. Today there will be four witnesses, the first two to be
called before lunch from the Australian Taxation Office: firstly, Mr Tyson Fawcett; secondly,
Mr Michael Kerr-Brown. The witnesses after lunch represent the Community and Public
Sector Union. It's convenient at this point if I tender the material to form the exhibits for the
day. There should be a draft exhibit list with you, Commissioner -
COMMISSIONER: Yes, there is.
MR GREGGERY: - commencing at 2032 and concluding at 2490, although it contains some
additional references to exhibits tendered earlier. I tender the bundle.
COMMISSIONER: Yes. Those documents numbered 2302 through to 2490 are admitted
bearing the exhibit numbers contained in the schedule. Thank you.
<EXHIBITS 2302 TO 2490 AS PER THE SCHEDULE TENDERED
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. Mr Tyson Fawcett is present.
COMMISSIONER: Yes. Mr Fawcett, would you prefer to take an oath or an affirmation?
MR FAWCETT: Affirmation, please.
<TYSON FAWCETT, AFFIRMED
<EXAMINATION BY MR GREGGERY:
COMMISSIONER: Thank you. Take a seat. Yes, Mr Greggery.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. Thank you. Mr Fawcett, you received a Notice to Give Evidence and
Produce Documents, NTG-0087, dated 21 November 2022 and produced a Statement in

MR FAWCETT: That's correct.
MR GREGGERY: And do you have a copy of the Notice and your Statement there - or at least
your Statement?
MR FAWCETT: I have a copy of my Statement, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. Alright. As you indicate in your Statement, you were first
employed by the Australian Taxation Office in May 1990?
MR FAWCETT: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: And have continued for a little over 32 years with the ATO?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct.
MR GREGGERY: You're currently the Senior Director, which is an Executive Level 2, in the
ATO Smarter Data Program data management team?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct.
MR GREGGERY: And who do you report to currently?
MR FAWCETT: So I currently report to the Assistant Commissioner -
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR FAWCETT: - inside of the Smarter Data Program referred to as Peter Phelps.
MR GREGGERY: And back in 2015 and 2016, who did you report to?
MR FAWCETT: Again, reported to then at the time an Assistant Commissioner. Back in about
2015, it would have been Paul McKenzie.
MR GREGGERY: And do I understand that you have held that role that you're currently in
since 2015; is that right?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, that would be correct.
MR GREGGERY: The responsibilities of the Smarter Data team include advising on data
sharing within key - or with key government agencies, which include Services Australia?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct.
MR GREGGERY: Was that always the case, that is, back in 2015 and 2016 as well?

MR FAWCETT: To the best in relation to what I can recall back in 2015 would largely be as it
did, and it still continues today in relation to working closely with Services Australia, yes. I
might only add that there are other parts in the Australian Taxation Office that also deal with
Services Australia as well.
MR GREGGERY: The focus of this inquiry is on the introduction of the manual
payment - sorry, the Manual Compliance program and the Online Compliance program in
2015 and 2016. You were involved to some extent in the dealings with Services Australia
during that period of time in respect of that program?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct.
MR GREGGERY: Who was your primary counterpart at Services Australia, then the
Department of Human Services?
MR FAWCETT: In 2015, and to my memory at the time, Ben Lumley was one of my key
counterparts in the Department of Human Services. To a lesser degree, Scott Britton and
Jason Ryman also, but there may have also been others who I came into contact with. But to
the best of my memory, they're the people I can remember.
MR GREGGERY: At paragraph 1.19 of your Statement, you identify that sometime between
September 2013 and mid-2015, you became aware that there were arrangements whereby
the ATO shared data with Services Australia and that had been a process which existed, at
least to the time you became aware of it, for a number of years. Do you recall the
circumstances in which you became aware of that?
MR FAWCETT: Between '13 and '15, that is?
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR FAWCETT: Not with absolute preciseness as to when I became aware of it, other than I
might just qualify that and say in 2015, of course, I began to be copied in on certain emails as
it directly related to the Department of Human Services and those sorts of things.
MR GREGGERY: And is that because the Smarter Data program was established within the
ATO in about 2015?
MR FAWCETT: I might just qualify that and say in the Smarter Data program, to my memory,
sort of occurred in sort of June 2015. But there may be copies of information that I had
received in relation to that Department of Human Services relation prior to June 2015.
MR GREGGERY: Right.
MR FAWCETT: So just to provide that chronology in that line.
MR GREGGERY: Yes. And do you think it was just from being copied into emails in that

MR FAWCETT: Yes, that is correct.
MR GREGGERY: Now, you came to know Mr Michael Kerr-Brown in about 2014/2015?
MR FAWCETT: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: What role did he have within the ATO in relation to your role?
MR FAWCETT: Can I just clarify, Counsel: is that in relation to the 2015 period we're talking
about?
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR FAWCETT: Yes. So best to describe that Michael had a role in relation to sort of reporting
to me -
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR FAWCETT: - at that particular point in time. I might just sort of clarify that there was
some organisational change going on between - being the Small Business and Individual
Taxpayer group moving to the Smarter Data group, which is that June 2015 period. So it's
sort of a movement between different things then.
MR GREGGERY: Right. To your understanding, did Mr Kerr-Brown have a more direct
day-to-day role in the interaction with Services Australia at that time?
MR FAWCETT: That would be correct in terms of the information I have reviewed as well.
MR GREGGERY: You refer in paragraph 1.24 to two forums, the Data Management Forum
and the Consultative Forum. Were you a regular attender of either or both of those?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, I might just provide some clarity around both forums just for people. In
relation to both forums, they're actually senior executive forums. In relation to the Data
Management Forum, that's a senior executive role, the Band 1. In relation to the
Consultative Forum, that's a Band 2. And in relation to my attendance at either of those
forums, it would often be - it could be in an ad hoc basis, because I'm not a senior executive
officer. So those forums are directly run by those people.
MR GREGGERY: But from time to time you attended, I gather from -
MR FAWCETT: Yes, that - sorry. To answer your question, that is correct.
MR GREGGERY: And was that on the basis that you were invited to speak to a particular issue
or address the forum in respect of a particular matter?

MR GREGGERY: Generally speaking?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, generally speaking.
MR GREGGERY: Now, as at about June 2015, what was your understanding of the legal
framework in which the ATO provided its data to Services Australia?
MR FAWCETT: So, to the best of my memory at the time, it was - and from documents I've
since sort of reviewed, the mechanism of exchange was the Data Matching Program, up
until - at least in that July 2015 period.
MR GREGGERY: That is, the Data-matching Program Act?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct. Apologies.
MR GREGGERY: Right. And is that because the data matched with - or provided by the ATO to
Centrelink or Services Australia was by - through the identification process which involved
Tax File Numbers?
MR FAWCETT: I'm unable to confirm whether that is the case, in relation to the use of Tax
File Numbers.
MR GREGGERY: Right.
MR FAWCETT: I just - generally in the context of data being shared under that Act as it
related to the Department of Human Services then at the time.
MR GREGGERY: You say based on documents that you have referred to since, that's your
understanding - or, rather, your memory and documents that you have referred to since.
Have you located any documents from the ATO perspective that - any documents which bear
out its own assessment of the basis on which ATO data was shared with Centrelink?
MR FAWCETT: In reference to the 2015 period onwards, is that the period you're referring
to?
MR GREGGERY: Yes.
MR FAWCETT: Yes, there has been the location of a number of documents referring to data
being shared back with the Department of Human Services in that period of time.
MR GREGGERY: A number of the documents you refer to in your Statement are emails from
Mr Lumley -
MR FAWCETT: Correct.

MR GREGGERY: - who indicates an intention to move away from the Data-matching Program
Act as the framework under which the data was supplied?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct.
MR GREGGERY: Apart from his assertion that there was a need to move away from the Act to
a less limiting process, have you identified any purely ATO documents, that is, not emails but
ATO records, policies, procedures, which deal with that proposition, the provision of data
under the Act?
MR FAWCETT: No, I haven't.
MR GREGGERY: So is it fair to say that the basis of your recollection that data was provided
by the ATO to Centrelink, that is, up to that mid-2015 period, is based really on assertions
contained in emails from Mr Lumley to the ATO which you have reviewed in the preparation
of your Statement?
MR FAWCETT: That would be correct.
MR GREGGERY: Okay. Does that suggest to your mind that the basis on which the ATO
shared data was really guided in large part by the nature of the request from Centrelink?
MR FAWCETT: I might just ask you to repeat that question, just so I understand what you're
saying.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. I might go back and deal with an earlier proposition, that is, if you
haven't been able to identify any internal - that is, ATO policy documents within the Smarter
Data program which deal with the basis on which ATO data is supplied, does that mean that
really it was Centrelink who was identifying the basis on which it requested data and,
therefore, the basis on which it was supplied?
MR FAWCETT: Well, I might - I think that's a correct proposition, other - I might just sort of
add in relation to the lead agencies sort of requesting as to the mechanism in which they
want to collect that data, we can - the Tax Office can be guided by that in that particular
circumstance, yes.
MR GREGGERY: That is, the ATO adopted a rather passive role in respect of the requests by
Centrelink for data and the purpose for which it would be used?
MR FAWCETT: I think that could be a correct assumption, yes.
MR GREGGERY: In paragraph 3.7 of your Statement, you identified by at least 18 January
2016, and possibly earlier, you were aware that the exception contained in section 355-65 of
Schedule 1 to the Taxation Administration Act permitted the ATO to share taxpayer
information, other than Tax File Numbers, with Services Australia where the disclosure was
for the purpose of administering social security law. And at paragraph 3.8, you continue that

you were aware of this based on the advice from Simon Murray to George Holton dated 18
January 2016. Now, if I just pause there, who was George Holton?
MR FAWCETT: So George Holton then at the time was Assistant Commissioner to whom I
reported to.
MR GREGGERY: And Simon Murray?
MR FAWCETT: Simon Murray, as I recall, worked in our General Counsel area in relation to
providing advice.
MR GREGGERY: We might just go to those documents. And the first is Exhibit 2337,
ATO.001.622.3075_R. This is the advice that you're referring to?
MR FAWCETT: That would be correct, I believe.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. If we just go to the bottom of page 1, you can see an email from
George Holton to a number of people, which include yourself, dated Thursday, 19 November
2015, which refers to:
...a summary below and accompanying draft instruction items resulting from Monday's
workshop with DHS.
You can see that?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, I can.
MR GREGGERY: And if we go over to the next page, there was discussion, it seems, about
strategic drivers for each agency and a significant degree of overlap. But at high level, there
was a number of dot points that both agencies were working to deliver. You can see that?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, I can, Counsel. I just haven't read it completely. That's all.
MR GREGGERY: No, that's okay. And please don't hesitate to ask for some additional time if
you would like to read a document.
MR HUTSON: Sorry.
MR GREGGERY: I take it, though, that this is one of the documents you reviewed in the
preparation of your Statement?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, it would be a document that I'm copied in to. As to reviewing it, it should
have been a document that I should have seen. Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. The summary of action items agreed to at the end of the workshop,
which had been conducted that week, included point 3, and that was that:

Each agency needs to develop and implement internal policy and business process that
ensures there is a single coordinating point for the management of exchange of information.
And that there would need to be a document, I think, or a documented process in respect of
agreed inter-agency policy that covered collection, management and exchange of data. Now,
if I just pause there, having refreshed your memory from this document in the preparation of
your Statement, do you recall whether there was, within the Smarter Data program, any step
towards the formalisation of the framework and process - that is, legal framework and
process for the provision of ATO data to DHS?
MR FAWCETT: Yes. In recalling that, I can't recall at the time whether that was done.
MR GREGGERY: And you haven't been able to identify, I take it, any document which records
this action item being implemented or the product of it?
MR FAWCETT: Apologies. No, I haven't.
MR GREGGERY: If we turn back to page 1, then. We can then see that you are, in the middle
of the page, sent the summary by Simon Murray on Monday, 18 January 2016. Perhaps if the
middle of the page could be pulled out there. Thank you.
MR FAWCETT: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: That's the date from which you make the reference in your Statement that
you were aware of these things as at that date?
MR FAWCETT: That's correct, Counsel. Yes.
MR GREGGERY: If I could go to Exhibit 2338, ATO.001.622.3077_R. For completeness, Mr
Fawcett, I will just refer you to the attachment. And this is, again, I guess, the formal advice
from Mr Murray to Mr Holton dated 18 January 2016 which was attached to that earlier
email. I know you're nodding, but it's being recorded so you just have to give a verbal -
MR FAWCETT: Yes. Apologies.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. And it sets out a reference particularly to the Taxation
Administration Act of 1953; identifies the general prohibition; the definition of "protected
information"; and the exception contained in subsection 355-65, sub (1) of Schedule 1 to the
Act. You can see that at the bottom of the page?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct.
MR GREGGERY: And that is that the general prohibition does not apply - if we go over to the
next page. Thank you. And call out paragraph 6 and the box below it. Sub (1) provides that
the general prohibition does not apply - and this was your understanding at the time - where
the disclosure is to an agency head - that would be a secretary of the Department of Human

Services - dealing with matters relating to the social security law, in column 2, and the record
or disclosure is for the purpose of administering that law?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct.
MR GREGGERY: And, again, that informed, in a technical sense or a legal sense, your
understanding of the basis on which disclosure, which would ostensibly be contrary to the
privacy provisions, was permitted by the Taxation Administration Act?
MR FAWCETT: That would be correct.
MR GREGGERY: Thank you. In preparation for your Statement, have you been able to identify
any requests, that is, documents requesting ATO data, for the purpose of administering the
social security law which refer to that provision?
MR FAWCETT: Not that I can recall, no.
MR GREGGERY: If we could return to your Statement at paragraph 3.11. It might be
convenient to bring it up on the screen. Exhibit 2303. Thank you. And if - thank you. Again,
Mr Fawcett, you set out your understanding or your awareness of the data-sharing process
between the ATO and Centrelink as at December 2015 in this paragraph?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct. As much as I knew, yes.
MR GREGGERY: And in identifying that you knew these things by at least December 2015, is
that based on your recollection at the time or your recollection in addition to documents you
have reviewed?
MR FAWCETT: It would be based on my recollections and documents I've since been able to
discover, yes.
MR GREGGERY: Yes, right. And you identify there that Services Australia provided a file to the
ATO containing a list of individuals and identifying information in respect of those individuals
which would then be applied or matched within the ATO data relating to those individuals?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct, yes.
MR GREGGERY: The way in which Services Australia provided a file, that was electronically, I
presume?
MR FAWCETT: To the best of my memory. I wouldn't have the preciseness of that or couldn't
even recall that.
MR GREGGERY: Okay.
MR FAWCETT: Yes.

MR GREGGERY: It might be that Mr Kerr-Brown is in a better position to identify some of the
intricacies of this process?
MR FAWCETT: I think that would be correct - be more precise.
MR GREGGERY: In addition to the bulk list or the multiple individual list you refer to in
subparagraph (a), there were also occasions, which you identify in paragraph 3.12, of
requests from Services Australia in respect of specific persons. Do you see that there in
paragraph 3.12?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, I can.
MR GREGGERY: Alright.
MR FAWCETT: It's not on my screen, but -
MR GREGGERY: You've got the hard copy, yes.
MR FAWCETT: Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. It's being brought up now. Again, you've not been able to identify
any - anything in writing which communicates that these requests were made, that is, a
document from DHS or Centrelink saying, pursuant to some particular provision of an Act,
they require information in respect of an individual?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, that would be correct. I've been unable to locate documents to that
effect.
MR GREGGERY: Again, given that you are not aware of the precise process, is it your
understanding that this was generally done electronically?
MR FAWCETT: It would be unfair of me to say whether it was done electronically or not. It's
not sort of the - I don't have the precise process.
MR GREGGERY: How was it that you became aware of these requests in respect of specified
individuals?
MR FAWCETT: I can't recall specifically at the time, but it seems to have been some
knowledge that I was aware of. I just can't tell you, Counsel, where it's - whether it was at
that very specific time that I became aware of that. That's all.
MR GREGGERY: And if we go down to paragraphs 3.13 and 3.14, you again describe in broad
terms your awareness of the purpose for which the information was requested as the
identification of discrepancies and reconciling against benefit entitlements?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, that's correct. I think I used the term "income compliance purposes" at

MR GREGGERY: But again, in your role, you had no understanding at any detailed level of
how Services Australia underwent that process - or undertook that process?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct.
MR GREGGERY: And if we go to paragraph 3.15, which spans the next two pages - thank
you - and call that out. Again, your awareness here that from July 2016, income data shared
by the ATO with Services Australia was no longer being shared under the Data Management
Program Act and that the relevant legislation was the Taxation Administration Act, to which
we referred. Is that awareness again in very broad terms from emails which you've identified
came from Centrelink or the Department of Human Services?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, that's correct, Counsel. Those earlier 2015 emails, it talks about the DMP.
MR GREGGERY: That is, there was a communication from Mr Lumley primarily that the
Department of Human Services wished to move away from the Act - the Data Management
Program Act and move to a more flexible arrangement?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct.
MR GREGGERY: If we go down to paragraph 4.3. This is again a reference to July 2016. The
data which you understood to be provided by the ATO as PAYG data was being shared twice
a year with Centrelink?
MR FAWCETT: That is correct.
MR GREGGERY: And it was data for the whole of the financial year, according to your
understanding?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, that's my understanding. Annual data.
MR GREGGERY: And your understanding is based - correct me if I'm wrong - on two things:
(1) what you've been told; and (2) your understanding that the Taxation Office collects PAYG
information from employers for a financial year?
MR FAWCETT: That's correct. We collect financial year data. Yes.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. Were you aware of any occasions where data was provided - PAYG
data related to a lesser period of time, that is, a period of some months throughout a
financial year?
MR FAWCETT: I'm probably unable to recall whether that was the case back then. I just can't
recall anything.
MR GREGGERY: And, again, if we go to paragraph 5.1. Thank you. The question was:

Provide, for each framework relevant examples of the requests made by the Agency...
That's Services Australia, formerly DHS:
...to the ATO to initiate [the] process.
But you've not been able to identify a file from Services Australia requesting data from the
ATO or the return file from the ATO responding to a request?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: Again, does that suggest a very high degree of automation in the transaction,
an online request by Services Australia and an online response between various computer
programs?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, I'm unable to advise on that. Like, I am unable to recall if there was
anything that was advised to me on those things.
COMMISSIONER: Another possibility is there isn't a request; it's just automatically sent
across. But you don't have that kind of information?
MR FAWCETT: No, I don't, Commissioner. Apologies.
MR GREGGERY: At any point through to about mid-2016, did you become concerned about
the legal basis on which the ATO was providing data to Centrelink in respect of the Online
Compliance program?
MR FAWCETT: There's nothing that I can recall specifically that raised any concerns with me.
MR GREGGERY: In your mind, were you assuming that because it had been done for a
number of years in a particular way that all of those questions must have been solved at an
earlier point in time?
MR FAWCETT: In my mind back in mid-2016, I am of the belief that the way I was thinking of
it, was that it was annualised income data being cross-checked with annual - or income data
being provided to DHS to then reconcile with the level of benefit that's been paid out. That's
a very long answer, apologies for that, but yes.
MR GREGGERY: That's alright.
COMMISSIONER: But what about the basis on which it was done? Did you think about that or
not? The legal basis, I mean.
MR FAWCETT: Commissioner, it's sort of a long-established relationship with the Department
of Human Services of which continued to carry over. So the answer is I don't recall whether I
turned my mind to those things at the time.

COMMISSIONER: And what Mr Greggery had suggested to you was to the effect that since
had it had been done for a long time, did you assume that somebody must have sorted it out
the basis on which it was done?
MR FAWCETT: Commissioner, I don't know whether I turned my mind to whether someone
had sorted it out. If - so apologies. But I think I was thinking it had been a long-established
process, as you said.
COMMISSIONER: Alright.
MR GREGGERY: I might just take you to a particular document, Exhibit 314,
ATO.0001.957.0908_R. Now, these are minutes from the DHS/ATO Data Management Forum
held 8 April 2016. You can see that on your screen there, Mr Fawcett?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, I can.
MR GREGGERY: And this was a meeting that you attended. You can see the list from the
ATO?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, I can see that I am listed as an attendee.
MR GREGGERY: If we go to the second page of the document. The debrief, which was agenda
item 3, if that could be called out. Sorry, that's 2. Just the one below it. Thank you. You were
describing the Consultative Forum debrief - that's the other Forum - and you updated this
particular Forum on that Forum's discussion on 19 February - that's 2016:
Milestones to date. The program of work. The work required by July 2016.
Can I just pause there. What's your recollection of what was being discussed at that
Consultative Forum and what you were updating this Forum about?
MR FAWCETT: I might just have a moment just to read it, if that's okay.
MR GREGGERY: Of course.
MR FAWCETT: Apologies. Apologies. Can I have the question again, Counsel?
MR GREGGERY: So I was just asking you whether the optimisation plan which was presented
to the Consultative Forum on 19 February related to - or what you recall that related to?
MR FAWCETT: Yes, I'm actually unable to recall what the actual optimisation plan is related
to out of the pieces - the action items that were being there.
MR GREGGERY: Alright. The suggestion that work was required by July 2016 indicates that
there was something which had to happen?

MR GREGGERY: Did this relate to the Online Compliance Intervention program?
MR FAWCETT: Again, I'm unable to recall whether it's actually related to that. But as you say,
it looks a lot like that it's relating to the Bulk Data Exchange of July 2016, to the best of what I
can see.
MR GREGGERY: Because your understanding was that at this point in time that the ATO
required Bulk Data Exchanges to start the OCI process?
MR FAWCETT: Sorry. DHS required to get Bulk Data Exchanges from the Tax Office to be able
to start that program. But I might just add, just for clarity, there are two topics of
optimisation occurring in many of these emails, and it just takes me some time to distinguish
between the two things. That's all.
MR GREGGERY: Not a problem at all, Mr Fawcett. When there is a reference to people in
Canberra from DHS taking an interest in the work, do you recall what that was about?
MR FAWCETT: Apologies. It's unclear to me who that's sort of referring to.
MR GREGGERY: And the Consultative Forum, I think you said that was an SES level forum?
MR FAWCETT: It's an SES Band 2 level forum, actually.
MR GREGGERY: SES Band - yes.
MR FAWCETT: Yes, that's correct.
MR GREGGERY: If we can go over to the next page and call out agenda item 4. The item was:
Data to support Budget Measures.
In the third line, you see that Tim Burgan from the ATO and others "landed a file yesterday"
and it's "progressing well"?
What does that mean?
MR FAWCETT: I just take time just to read it, if that's okay.
MR GREGGERY: Of course.
MR FAWCETT: Sorry. The question again, Counsel?
MR GREGGERY: What does "landing a file yesterday which is progressing well" mean?
MR FAWCETT: I have no specifics about precisely what occurred at that time. But just reading

MR GREGGERY: That is, one of the requests for data?
MR FAWCETT: Look - requests for data in the bulk file, you're referring to, or -
MR GREGGERY: You've described it as something from DHS.
MR FAWCETT: I'm unable to - I'm unable to recognise -
MR GREGGERY: Sorry, from the Tax Office to DHS.
MR FAWCETT: Yes. Correct. Sorry. I see.
MR GREGGERY: It was clear at this point, though, that your understanding of what was being
proposed was the provision of a large sample file without Tax File Numbers?
MR FAWCETT: Yes. What I can read from here, it’s provisions for the landing of a file without
Tax File Numbers.
MR GREGGERY: And that's quantified by the reference to 100,000 - the number 100,000?
MR FAWCETT: Yes. Again, I can only reference what I see in front of me here. Yes.
MR GREGGERY: You're noted as questioning whether legislative change was being sought.
Why did you ask that question?
MR FAWCETT: Without understanding - not having the preciseness of what occurred at that
time only leads me to believe it was a question more related to use of Tax File Numbers and
amendments around that. But, again, I don't have preciseness around what occurred at that
time.
MR GREGGERY: It appeared to be a discussion also in respect of - one which related to the
privacy rules. You can see that?
